title: Pāṭala L0 — character-class coverage taxonomy
description: Defines what 'lossless' means for L0. Not 'every character belongs to a token' but: 'every SEMANTICALLY relevant source character is either represented by an L0 token or explicitly classified as STRUCTURAL non-semantic material.' Any character left UNKNOWN is a coverage failure.

SEMANTIC.description: scholarly content that MUST be represented by an L0 token (the gloss/lemma stream)

STRUCTURAL.description: non-semantic markdown/syntax that is explicitly classified and permitted between tokens

classes.marker: the '[and]-' token prefix marker (structural, not content)
classes.quote: quotation marks '" " ' that wrap quoted spans

IGNORED_WITH_REASON.description: explicitly non-semantic material outside the token stream with a recorded reason

UNKNOWN.description: any character not token-covered and not classified above — a HARD FAILURE (potential real content loss)

proof_invariants.no_overlap: no two tokens share a character
proof_invariants.no_duplicate: no two tokens have identical spans
proof_invariants.monotonic: token spans are strictly increasing in chunk_char_start
proof_invariants.coverage: no character classified UNKNOWN (every semantic char token-covered or STRUCTURAL/IGNORED_WITH_REASON)
